title: Teaching the Plan of Salvation (Part 1)
focus: Practice topic: the purpose of life on earth
intro: God has a plan for His children. In this lesson learners study our life before earth, the purpose of mortality, and the Fall of Adam and Eve, then practise teaching these truths simply.
preparation: Study 2 Nephi 2:22–25, Alma 12:32–34 and Moses 1:39. Be ready to play a video on our Father in Heaven and one on the plan of salvation. Have the hymn “I Am a Child of God” (Hymns, no. 301) ready. Pray for each learner by name.

sections.title: Before this life
paras: Read the words of “I Am a Child of God” (Hymns, no. 301) together, then sing it. Ask what the words teach about life before earth and the purpose of life here.

Read President Boyd K. Packer’s thoughts on who we are and what we lived before. Ask how knowing we lived as God’s spirit children changes the way we see ourselves and others. Teach the truth: when we know we are children of God, our lives gain meaning and purpose. Ask learners to share how this knowledge has helped them.

sections.title: God’s plan for His children
paras: Read Moses 1:39 and memorize it together. Ask what God’s work and glory is. Draw out the truth: God’s plan is to help His children become like Him and have eternal life.

Read what Sister Susan W. Tanner taught in “The Sanctity of the Body,” Ensign or Liahona, November 2005: we shouted for joy to take part in this plan, and a physical body is a key step toward becoming like our Father (see Job 38:7; Doctrine and Covenants 130:22; 93:33). Ask what we understood before earth that made us eager to come, even knowing the trials.

sections.title: Agency and the Fall
paras: Draw two columns, one before the Fall and one after. Let learners study 2 Nephi 2:22–25 and fill them in. In the garden, Adam and Eve could not have children or know joy and sorrow. After the Fall, they could choose, grow and become parents.

Ask why the Fall is a vital part of God’s plan, and why mortality is needed to receive the blessings He wants for us. Read Moses 1:39 again. Review how to teach the Fall without blame, as a step in God’s plan.

sections.title: Our life on earth
paras: Read President Packer’s three-act play comparison in “The Play and the Plan,” Church Educational System fireside, May 1995, or watch the video on the plan of salvation. Act 1 is before earth, act 2 is mortality and act 3 is after death. We are on stage in the middle of act 2 without remembering act 1.

Ask why the play explains why people find it hard to know the purpose of life. Ask where the script is found. Draw out the answer: the scriptures. Ask how scripture helps God’s children understand their purpose.

sections.title: Overcoming sin and death
paras: Explain that this life is a time to prepare to meet God (see Alma 12:32–34). Write on the board: Consequences of sin. Ask what they are, and how understanding them prepares someone to accept the Atonement. Draw out the truth: sin separates us from God, and the gospel of Jesus Christ lets us be forgiven and return.

Ask how you would explain the purpose of life in one or two sentences. Then pair learners to prepare a five-to-ten-minute lesson, using their own words and scripture. Afterward, ask what each pair did well and what could be better.

steps.why: Teach the idea and why it matters for a missionary.

examples.title: Name the three acts
examples.text: Draw three acts on the board: before earth, mortality and after death. Show one verse for each.

examples.title: Show why we came
examples.text: Read Moses 1:39 and 2 Nephi 2:25. Explain in your own words why we came to earth.

examples.title: Explain the Fall as a step
examples.text: Use a two-column chart to show life before and after the Fall. Show how it opened the way to choice and joy.

steps.why: Show one example of what learners will do.

examples.title: Teach the purpose of life in three minutes
examples.text: Say who we are, why we came and how the Savior helps us return. Read Moses 1:39 and testify.

examples.title: Teach the Fall without blame
examples.text: Show how to explain the Fall as part of God’s plan and not as a failure.

examples.title: Show the three-act play
examples.text: Use the play to explain the plan simply. Ask a friend where the script is found.

steps.why: Learners practise in pairs or small groups.

examples.title: Teach in pairs
examples.text: Each pair prepares and teaches a five-minute lesson on the purpose of life, using scripture and testimony.

examples.title: Answer a question
examples.text: A friend asks, “Why would God send us here to suffer?” Answer with the plan of salvation and a verse.

examples.title: Draw it out
examples.text: Each learner draws the plan on paper and explains it to a partner.

steps.why: Name what went well and what can improve.

examples.title: Partner feedback
examples.text: The learner who was taught says what was clearest and what felt most sincere. The teacher writes one thing to keep and one to improve.

examples.title: Three questions
examples.text: Ask: What went well? What would you change? What helped the listener most to understand the purpose of life? Begin with the good.

examples.title: Simple checklist
examples.text: Was it simple? Was a scripture used and explained? Was the listener invited to act? Did the teacher speak with sincerity?

steps.why: Practise again with what was learned.

examples.title: Switch roles
examples.text: The learner who listened now teaches. Leave time for feedback both ways, then ask a few to share what they learned.

examples.title: Improve one thing
examples.text: Each learner teaches again and changes one thing from the feedback: a clearer sentence, a better scripture or a warmer invitation.

examples.title: Teach a new partner
examples.text: Find a new partner. Teach the same lesson again in a few minutes. Share one insight with the class.

testimony: Testify that God knows each person and that His plan brings joy. Invite learners to share what the plan means to them.

tips.text: Help learners memorize one key verse. Expect different abilities and be kind about it.
Use a story or a picture to explain a big idea.
Let pairs teach each other, then ask what worked.
Ask learners to look for a truth before reading a scripture.

Write an outline to teach the plan of salvation. Teach it to a friend and write what you learned.
